tasks.commitBody: The collective gets its Lingikogu: a links page where admins curate an ordered list of named URLs and members read it, the first surface for the link type provisioned live on both databases earlier today. The list renders in its stored order; admins add, edit in place, remove, and reorder with plain native buttons, and the reordering persists through the same atomic renumber the section list already uses, because links and sections parent identically off the collective root. Members see the list and none of the controls — absent, not disabled, like every tiered control in the app. URLs are stored and rendered exactly as typed: no scheme-guessing, no normalising, and the only validation anywhere is that a name and a URL are non-empty, because the sign-off ruled guessing user intent out of scope. A link without a description simply has no description line. The page is the app's seventh navigation entry, named in all four locales, and carries the collective-switch generation guard from the shared route-load machine so a stale read from the previous collective can never populate the next one's list. Entering Joosep's recordings archive into it is ordinary product use by an admin, per the ruling that closed the authorization question on the issue. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.

THE CONTRACT: a per-season entry point, NOT a picker (dropdown/select explicitly rejected). Done-when: (1) admin can open the management panel for ANY upcoming season they hold rights on, not just the soonest; (2) the panel states WHICH season it is managing, visibly, whenever more than one is manageable; (3) switching the managed season leaves NO stale state — repertoire, series rows, in-flight writes belong to the open season ('a context switch and behaves like one'); (4) rights are RE-DERIVED per season — manageableSeasonRights never carried across a switch; (5) existing behaviour BYTE-IDENTICAL when only one season is manageable — no new control in the common case.

BAKED SHAPE (from research; deviations are GREEN's to state):
- The manageable SET: every not-lapsed season (current + upcoming) where the viewer's per-season rights resolve to editor. Per-season owners/editors already ride on every Season from listSeasons (research 2d) — derive per season via the extracted manageRightsFrom helper. The DB-entity-rights fallback (+page.svelte:958-991) is COLLECTIVE-level — when it promotes, it promotes uniformly for all candidate seasons (state this in a comment at the site).
- Rendering: the single collapsed season card block becomes an iteration over the manageable set — one collapsed card per season, each opening the panel FOR THAT season. With exactly one manageable season the rendered output is the current one, byte-identical (criterion 5 — pin by asserting the single-season DOM unchanged against the existing season-card specs' expectations).
- Season switch = context switch: opening season B while A is open runs the full reset (resetSeasonManage-shape) then loads B. seasonManageFieldsLoaded is a plain boolean reseed guard at +page.svelte:3072 — it MUST not leak A's fields under B's heading (reset on switch; season-keying is GREEN's choice, state it).
- Guard idiom: a NEW in-file generation ticket bumped when the managed season changes, sibling to requestId/worksLoadId/scheduleLoadId (+page.svelte:701-729) — the blast finding is explicit: extend the in-file sibling pattern, do NOT import routeLoad.ts into +page.svelte. The known unguarded handlers (research 2b: confirmSeasonFieldEdit, onSeasonManageConductorSelect/Remove at :3250-3350 capture seasonId but mutate shared state with NO live re-check on resolve) become REACHABLE bugs the moment two seasons are manageable — pin them: a field edit resolving after a season switch must not write into the new season's panel state.
- manageableSeason(seasons, now) in conductorLogic.ts:104 and its 12-case spec DO NOT change — the automatic pick remains the default; #277 adds an override, not a different default (research finding 5 says those specs must NOT flip).

PINS:
1. Two manageable seasons → two collapsed entries, each names its season; one manageable → EXACTLY today's DOM (no wrapper changes, no new testids in the single case if avoidable — state if unavoidable).
2. Opening season B's entry loads B's series + repertoire + fields; panel heading names B (criterion 2's visible label — new i18n key in all four locales if a new string is needed).

THE RACE PINS (the issue's own watch-for): (a) series read for A in flight when admin switches to B → never repopulates B's panel; (b) field edit on A resolving after switch to B → B's state untouched, no error leak into B's error slots; (c) in-flight conductor change on A → same isolation; (d) delete-arm state on A → disarmed by the switch (resetSeasonManage covers it — pin it stays covered).
4. Rights re-derivation: a viewer who is editor on A but not on B sees A's entry only; switching cannot carry A's 'editor' onto B (criterion 4).
5. Viewer with rights on zero seasons: no entries, no panel (absent not disabled).
6. Season-create still works and the new season joins the manageable set on reload (existing reload path).
7. Spec disposition (research finding 5): page.season-manage.spec.ts entry-point tests extend for the multi-season case; page.season-card.spec.ts '#261' pins survive for the single-season case; conductorLogic.manageable.spec.ts UNTOUCHED.

tasks.commitBody: Season management no longer belongs only to the soonest season: every upcoming season the admin holds editor rights on now has its own entry into the management panel — its own way in, not a picker, because choosing from the season you are looking at beats a dropdown duplicating the list beside it. With one manageable season nothing changes at all: the entry renders exactly as the single card always has, and the automatic soonest-season pick keeps its logic and its twelve-case spec untouched, since this adds an override, not a different default. Opening another season is a context switch and behaves like one — the panel resets wholesale, loads the new season's fields, series and repertoire under a heading that names it, and a new page-level generation ticket, sibling to the collective-switch counter the page already trusts, makes sure nothing in flight for the old season can land in the new one. That guard also closes a set of latent races that were unreachable while only one season could ever be managed: field edits and conductor changes that captured their season id but never re-checked it on resolve now do, because two manageable seasons is exactly the state that would have made them bite. Rights are re-derived per season from the owners and editors each season already carries, so being editor on one season shows that season's entry and no other's, and the collective-level rights fallback promotes uniformly for the same reason it exists at all — database-entity rights don't vary by season. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.
